classification.classification_note: The reproduced ASan finding is a global-buffer-overflow read in `xmlDictHashName`. The upstream fix commit message is `malloc-fail: Don't truncate parser input buffer`, and the staged witness also carries a 37-allocation fuzz budget that drives the parser into the malloc-failure error path before QName hashing.

bug_description.original: A global-buffer-overflow READ occurs in xmlDictHashName (dict.c), triggered during NCName/QName parsing (xmlParseNCName/xmlParseQNameHashed in parser.c). The hash/name lookup reads one byte out-of-bounds before the global table xmlIsPubidChar_tab (chvalid.c), which can lead to crashes or potential information disclosure when processing specially crafted XML names (e.g., element or attribute names).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree / upstream fix commit 8e13133d
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is a fuzz-framed XML input, not a plain XML file. Its header sets `maxAlloc` to 37 and its main entity is a 197-byte memory buffer whose first four bytes are `00 00 00 3c`, so libxml2 auto-detects UCS-4BE and enters document parsing on decoded `<...` content. During later lookahead growth on the QName path, a malloc-failure leaves the parser input buffer in an error state. Vulnerable `xmlBufResetInput` and `xmlBufUpdateInput` react by truncating `input->base`, `input->cur`, and `input->end` to the global empty-string literal instead of preserving the old buffer. `xmlParseNCNameComplex` can then combine a pre-failure offset with the new `BASE_PTR`, pass a pointer into that global empty string to dictionary hashing, and `xmlDictHashName` reads one byte past the 1-byte literal `""`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled main XML entity into libxml2 parser state.
source.value_from: The harness in `fuzz/xml.c` reads the first fuzz integer as parser options (`0x20202020`), the second fuzz integer as a raw allocation budget (`35649`), reduces that budget to `35649 % (207 + 100) = 37`, decodes an empty URL string, and decodes a 197-byte main entity `00 00 00 3c` followed by 193 literal space bytes before calling `xmlCtxtReadMemory(ctxt, docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts)`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The dictionary hash loop dereferences a name pointer that was rebound onto the global empty-string literal after malloc-failure input truncation.
sink.note: The saved ASan report records `global-buffer-overflow` at `dict.c:471` and places the faulting byte `0 bytes after` the global empty string literal defined in `buf.c`.

root_cause.description: On buffer error, the parser input is truncated to the global empty-string literal instead of preserving the previous buffer content and offsets.
root_cause.note: Upstream fix commit `8e13133d` is titled `malloc-fail: Don't truncate parser input buffer` and removes this same sentinel-truncation behavior from both `xmlBufUpdateInput` and `xmlBufResetInput`.

tainted_value_origin.var: data, size, opts, maxAlloc, docBuffer, docSize
tainted_value_origin.note: The harness both supplies the XML bytes and activates malloc-failure injection with the exact 37-allocation limit used by this witness.

parser_admitted.description: After `xmlDetectEncoding` has interpreted the witness prefix `00 00 00 3c` as UCS-4BE and switched decoding, the document parser reaches the start-tag gate with decoded `RAW == '<'` instead of rejecting the input as empty or non-XML.

coarse_trace.summary: libxml2 materializes the 197-byte main entity as a memory-backed parser input while the harness has already set the malloc-failure limit to 37.
The bytes `00 00 00 3c` are recognized as UCS-4BE, decoded into a document starting with `<`, and admitted into normal element parsing.
While the parser is on the QName path, a refill under the 37-allocation budget fails and leaves the underlying xmlBuf in `XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY` state.
Vulnerable error handling truncates the parser input to the global empty-string literal instead of keeping the old buffer alive.
The QName parser recombines a pre-failure buffer offset with the now-truncated `BASE_PTR` and forwards that bogus name pointer plus a positive length to dictionary lookup.
The hash loop dereferences one byte past the 1-byte global empty string, producing the saved global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled main entity is materialized as a memory-backed parser input. For this witness the entity length is 197 bytes and the harness has already reduced the raw fuzz budget `35649` to `maxAlloc == 37` before entering libxml2.
The first four entity bytes `00 00 00 3c` are interpreted as UCS-4BE, creating the decoding state that turns the witness into a document beginning with `<` instead of a raw NUL-prefixed byte stream.
The parser switches the memory input to the detected UCS-4BE decoder, so `xmlParseDocument` later reaches the start-tag path and calls `xmlParseElement(ctxt)` on decoded document content.
On the crashing QName path, the complex NCName parser snapshots the current offset within the live parser buffer. This offset is later recombined with `BASE_PTR` at dictionary lookup time.
Because lookahead falls below `INPUT_CHUNK`, character decoding requests more bytes from the same parser input during NCName parsing.
Under the witness's `maxAlloc == 37` malloc-failure budget, this refill path fails, so the buffered parser input enters an out-of-memory error state before the QName parse has finished.

Root-cause step. After the refill failure leaves `buf->error` set, vulnerable input-update logic truncates the parser input to the global empty-string literal instead of preserving the old buffer and offsets. The upstream fix removes this truncation behavior.

The QName parser uses the previously captured offset together with the now-truncated `BASE_PTR`. That transforms an offset into the real parser buffer into a pointer into the global empty-string object while still forwarding a positive maximum length to dictionary lookup.
Dictionary lookup trusts the corrupted name pointer from step 8 and uses the supplied NCName length as the hash loop bound.
Sink. The hash loop dereferences bytes from the global empty-string literal as if it were a real NCName buffer. ASan records the first invalid read immediately past that 1-byte object.

poc.trigger: The saved testcase is a fuzz-framed `xml` target input. Bytes `0..3` are parser options `0x20202020`; bytes `4..7` are the raw allocation-limit integer `35649`, which the harness reduces to `37`; the next fuzz string is the empty main URL; the next fuzz string is the exact 197-byte main entity `00 00 00 3c` followed by 193 literal `0x20` bytes.

format.name: libxml2-xml-fuzzer
format.contract: A libxml2 `fuzz/xml.c` testcase whose second 4-byte field yields `maxAlloc == 37` and whose first entity begins with the exact 4-byte UCS-4BE prefix `00 00 00 3c`. This witness couples malloc-failure injection with a decoded XML start-tag path; the validated trigger is this exact framed input, not a generic class of ordinary XML files.
